title: Meeting Rooms
statement: Given the `[start, end]` times of meetings, return `True` if one person could attend **all** of them, that is, if no two meetings overlap. A meeting may start exactly when another one ends.

example.why: The meeting [7, 10] is still running when [9, 12] starts.

idea: Comparing every pair of meetings would take O(n²). **Sort by start time** instead.
After sorting, a clash can only happen between **neighbours**: if a meeting overlaps any earlier one, it overlaps the one directly before it or that one already clashed.
So one pass is enough: a meeting that starts before the previous one has ended means `False`.

complexity.timeWhy: Sorting; the check itself is one pass.

steps.text: Our example: **`intervals = [[7,10],[0,5],[9,12]]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
Sort the meetings by start time. Now each meeting only needs to be compared with the one right before it.
[7, 10] starts at 7, when [0, 5] has already ended (5). No clash.
[9, 12] starts at 9, but the meeting before it, [7, 10], runs until 10. They **overlap**.
Two meetings overlap, so one person cannot attend them all → **False**.
Done — the answer is **`False`**. The meeting [7, 10] is still running when [9, 12] starts.
